messages:
Sam B: heads up — saw a p99 tail spike in canary this morning at ~600 QPS. looks like kernel fallback + kv-cache churn. attaching quick profiler dump. anyone on call? :eyes:
Nisha K: Oof. which model and seq length distribution?
Sam B: gpt-medium-ish (open variant), avg seq 120 but 15% > 512. fallback to fp16 kernels on those long requests. p95 fine, p99 jumps ~2.5x.
Liam R: does the kv cache eviction correlate? if requests with >512 tokens flush kv then everyone pays.
Sam B: profiler shows frequent cache misses and syncs at the longer-seq requests. interestingly kernel choice changes right after a miss.
Jenny H: can you paste the microbatch config? might be autoscaling batcher switching sizes under load.
Sam B: here: ```
microbatch_size: 8
max_batch_tokens: 4096
kernel_pref: [optimized_f16, fallback_f32]
admission_threshold: 0.85
```
Oliver M: admission_threshold 0.85 is aggressive — with that + microbatch=8 you can saturate GPUs then have load-shedding kicks in, causing tail rebuilds.
Nisha K: agree. If GPU util hits target, admission will queue or shed. But KV cache churn makes effective per-request time variable => headroom buffer should be larger.
Liam R: what are current GPU util numbers during the spike?
Sam B: 94% p50, p95 97% but jumps to 99% at the tail.
Jenny H: yeah that's nearly full. We usually aim for 70-80% to keep headroom for tails.
Liam R: have we tried adaptive microbatch sizing based on seq len? small seq -> larger batch, long seq -> isolate into smaller batches with kernel pinned.
Nisha K: we experimented with that — but schedule overhead caused latency regressions for p50 unless we limit to >256 tokens.
Sam B: perf-bot: attach profiler link 
perf-bot: profiler dump uploaded: https://ci.internal/perf/1792104567/dump1
Oliver M: quick experiment: lower admission_threshold to 0.7 and set kernel_pref to prefer stable kernels for long seqs. Also increase min_headroom_ms to 30 ms.
Jenny H: let's not drop admission_threshold without testing — that reduces throughput significantly. Maybe try dynamic admission: keep 0.85 but allow burst headroom when cache miss rate > X%.
Liam R: propose A/B: config A = admission 0.7, microbatch 8; config B = admission 0.85 + dynamic headroom rule + adaptive microbatch by seq len. Run 30m canary at target QPS.
Nisha K: +1. Also log KV cache hit/miss per request and attach to traces so we can correlate exact calls that trigger kernel fallback.
Sam B: adding log flags now. command: `./run_canary --config=canary_b.json --qps=600 --duration=1800`
Oliver M: can we also try switching kernel_pref order to prefer fp32 for >512 tokens to avoid runtime fallback cost?
Jenny H: that would add token cost but maybe reduces p99 latency. worth measuring.
Sam B: scheduled both experiments. canary A starts in 5m. collecting p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, kernel-switch counts.
Liam R: if p99 still bad, we should look at load-shedding policy. current shedding is drop-random; maybe better to reject longest requests first or queue them with lower priority.
Nisha K: agreed — latency SLOs for short interactive requests should be prioritized over long completion jobs. implement priority classes.
Oliver M: FYI I've seen cases where model compilation cache eviction caused kernel fallback cost > 50ms. ensure kernel binary cache not thrashing on the worker nodes.
Jenny H: ops, check node-level /var/cache/model-kernels disk usage. if eviction happening due to low disk, we get these weird fallbacks.
Sam B: noted. adding node cache metrics to the canary dashboard.
perf-bot: canary A (admission 0.7) finished — p99 reduced by ~18% but p50 throughput dropped ~12%
perf-bot: canary B (dynamic headroom) finished — p99 reduced by ~22% and p50 throughput change +2%
Liam R: wow canary B looks better. any change in kv hit rate?
Sam B: kv hit rate improved slightly (cache prefetch tweak) and kernel-switch count dropped 40% in B.
Nisha K: ok greenlight to roll B to production small ring, but keep monitoring admissions and node kernel cache metrics.
Jenny H: also add automated alert if p99 > 1.8x SLO or kernel-switch spikes > 20% in 5m window.
Oliver M: and schedule a follow-up to evaluate load-shedding policy for mixed workloads — long vs interactive.
Sam B: thanks all. I'll post the rollout plan and link to the dashboard. :rocket:
